item.desc: China can be amazing, but there are things nobody prepares you for. You can live here for years, study, work and build a life here — but your foreign passport can still make simple things complicated. Some hotels won’t accept foreigners, some landlords don’t want foreign tenants, and the cameras are EVERYWHERE. As a student, your university can have strict rules around travel and activities. And WeChat? There are certain things you simply cannot freely post or discuss. Then there are the everyday experiences: booking a taxi and having the driver cancel after seeing you’re foreign, people staring, taking pictures without permission, touching your hair, or treating you differently because you’re Black. China has given me beautiful experiences, but also uncomfortable ones. These are the things I wish someone told me before moving here. 🇨🇳🤍 #ChinaLife #LivingInChina  #StudyInChina #lifeinchina

contents.desc: China can be amazing, but there are things nobody prepares you for.

You can live here for years, study, work and build a life here — but your foreign passport can still make simple things complicated. Some hotels won’t accept foreigners, some landlords don’t want foreign tenants, and the cameras are EVERYWHERE.
As a student, your university can have strict rules around travel and activities. And WeChat? There are certain things you simply cannot freely post or discuss.

Then there are the everyday experiences: booking a taxi and having the driver cancel after seeing you’re foreign, people staring, taking pictures without permission, touching your hair, or treating you differently because you’re Black.
China has given me beautiful experiences, but also uncomfortable ones.
These are the things I wish someone told me before moving here. 🇨🇳🤍

item.desc: Seven close friends in China decided to build their dream home so they could retire and live together. They found a spot in the countryside near Guangzhou and spent around 4 million yuan (about $580,000 USD) to construct a spacious and peaceful mansion surrounded by nature. The house has large glass windows, open common areas, individual bedrooms for each of them, and a shared kitchen. They even included a tea pavilion where they can gather, drink tea, and enjoy each other's company. The idea came from a casual conversation, but they made it real by combining their savings and working closely with designers. They also made a plan for the future: they'll take care of one another as they grow older and even hire a cook and caretaker if needed. Their dream was to grow old together not in isolation, but with laughter, support, and lifelong friendship. #fyp #blowup #friends #story

The friends also reportedly agreed to learn skills such as cooking and gardening to make the experience more self-sustaining and enjoyable.

contents.desc: Living in China: What I Wish I Knew Before! 🇨🇳

Moving to China has been an adventure! 🌏 Here are some things I wish I knew before landing: You’ll need internet right away since many Western apps are blocked. People might stare, but they’re friendly! English isn’t common, so a translator is a must. Everything is super organized and clean, but watch out for hidden payment fees with foreign cards. Be ready for some surprises, like squat toilets and a mix of digital and traditional life. And don’t forget to download WeChat and Alipay before you come – they’re essential for daily life! The food? It’s a wild ride; you’ll either love it or get tired of it quickly.
